transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is most likely an intermittent electrical earth fault, not a programme or loading issue. A heater element beginning to leak to earth is the commonest cause if it trips a few minutes into the wash, once heating begins. If it trips during filling, draining or spin, the pump, motor wiring, mains filter or damp wiring become more likely. Do not use the machine again or keep resetting the kitchen breaker to retry it; it needs a qualified appliance engineer/electrician to diagnose and repair it. With the machine switched off and unplugged, you can safely look for obvious clues only:
1. Check the plug and visible mains lead for cuts, scorching, looseness or crushing. Any damage means leave it unplugged.
2. Look around the floor and accessible connections for signs of a leak or water underneath. Moisture can cause an intermittent trip.
3. Note the point in the cycle when it has tripped before — that is the most useful clue for the engineer. Does it normally trip as soon as it is switched on, while filling, a few minutes into washing, or on draining/spin?

Thanks, I've written that down. To answer your third point, it always trips a few minutes into a 40 or 60 degree wash. It has never tripped on a cold wash, the quick 30, or rinse and spin. It happens roughly 1 in 4 washes over the last month, and nothing unusual is heard beforehand.

I should be honest that I've been resetting the switch and carrying on each time, and it has tripped a good few times now. There's no burning smell and I haven't seen any sparking. The plug looks fine and isn't warm, and I haven't looked inside the machine.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The timing makes the heater element the clear leading suspect: it is likely leaking electricity to earth only when the machine starts heating. That fits 40°C/60°C washes tripping a few minutes in, while cold, quick and rinse/spin programmes do not. It still must remain unplugged and be checked by a qualified appliance engineer; repeated tripping can worsen an electrical fault. The engineer should insulation-test the heater and then check its wiring/connectors for dampness or damage before condemning any part. A mains filter or motor fault is much less likely from this pattern. With it switched off and unplugged only, have a look underneath and around the accessible hoses for any water staining or dampness. If there is any, tell the engineer, as moisture around wiring can produce the same intermittent earth-leakage symptom.

candidates: Heater element leaking to earth when the wash reaches its heating stage (high)
Drain pump, motor circuit, mains filter or wiring fault (medium)
Damaged mains lead/plug or moisture around the appliance connections (low)

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Indesit; model IWE 7 SOMETHING.
The fault they reported is: "Intermittently trips the kitchen power when running". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
